title: The six-piece band at Baron Wilkins
summary: He lists Elmer Chambers, Charley Dixon, Roland Smith, Walter Edwards and Joey Young, and tells about trombonists Revis Horton and Jimmy Harrison.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Okay, so you came to New York and you started working at Baron Wilkins. What was your band at this point. Did you have Charley Gaines with you?
No, I had Elmer Chambers.
Oh, I thought he had left you when you left Detroit.
No, he left me when we got to New York.
Oh, I see, so he came to New York with
you. He had been with you in Atlantic City, then.
He had been with me. He had been in Chicago, in Detroit with me, Atlantic City with me. And now we were going to New York.
Right.
He still played with me.
And Charley Dixon was still with you?
Yeah, Charley Dixon was there.
And who else?
But not Jimmy Harrison. No, Jimmy Harrison stayed out West this time.
Uh hunh.

He didn't come back from Detroit with us. He stayed out there. And I had a fellow called Revis Horton. He was a good trombone player. But, it's like I say with all trombone players, they're half nuts. You see. And he was -- Jimmy Harrison -- you see, nothing vicious about either one of them. But, Revis Horton, at that time, he didn't like white people. And Jimmy Harrison, he couldn't stop laughing. He laughed all the time. He told me he got fired off a job for laughing. The boss would look at him and say, 'You laugh too much. You take your hat and get out of here.'
(laugh)
But, see, they were both of them good trombone players.
So, how big a band did you have at Baron Wilkins?
Well now, let me see. There was a guitar, bass -- guitar, drum, piano, no bass. Clarinet, trumpet, and saxophone.
Uh hunh.
That was six. Six pieces.
Who was the saxophone player? Was that the --
The saxophone player was a fellow named Rollem Roland Smith.
Uh hunh.
And the clarinet player was a man named Edwards. We used to call him Mr. Edwards. [WALTER EDWARDS]
The West Indian.
Yeah, he was the West Indian fellow.
Right.
Yeah, see, so, -- and the rest of them were, you know -- Joey Young, he was on the drums. And Charley Dixon on guitar -- oh, banjoe, tenor banjo, there was no guitar in those days.
